relations.rationale: The friendly nods before the first round is a minor sequential detail that neither implies nor prevents rounds rotating pairings.
Wren being taller than Jude does not determine or prevent Xavi being taller than both by a margin, though both discuss relative heights.
Height comparison between Wren and Jude has no bearing on Xavi and Mina's ages.
Wren and Jude's height difference is unrelated to Xavi and Mina's ages relative to Fay.
Height comparison between Wren and Jude has no bearing on house membership of Mina and Jude.
Xavi's height relative to Wren and Jude does not relate to Xavi and Mina's ages.
Height comparisons do not bear on age comparisons.
Fay and Jude being in different houses does not determine whether Mina and Jude are in different houses.
Fay and Jude being in different houses supports the existence of multiple houses, consistent with there being three.
Rounds rotating and pairings changing sets up the context of comparing standings later, supporting that such a comparison would occur.
Xavi and Mina being close in age directly supports the more specific claim that they are both a year older than Fay.
Xavi and Mina being close in age doesn't specify their ages relative to Fay, so it doesn't confirm Fay is youngest.
If Xavi and Mina are both a year older than Fay, this supports Fay being the youngest among them.
Age relationships between Xavi, Mina, and Fay have no bearing on comparing standings on a chalkboard.
Fay being the youngest has no bearing on players comparing standings on a chalkboard.
Mina and Jude being in different houses supports the existence of multiple houses, consistent with three houses.
Comparing standings near the end naturally precedes and is consistent with helping clean up as the session wound down.
